upstream_test: custom: User approved decoupling crystal matching and elastic energy tests. A fixed-frame isotropic elastic example isolates energy from enumeration-dependent orientations.
configuration: Single fixed (001) cubic Si geometry, two sites, lattice 5.431 angstrom; isotropic Lamé constants lambda=100 GPa and mu=80 GPa; in-plane x stretch 1.02. Calls SubstrateMatch.from_zsl with explicit vectors, without lattice enumeration.
observable: Elastic energy in eV/atom and dimensionless von Mises strain, in that fixed order
default_vs_upstream: custom: user-approved isolated energy test; no upstream default is claimed
variant: stretch_x is replaced by its second binary64 successor: 1.02 to 1.0200000000000005; the geometry frame and isotropic stiffness remain fixed.
altbuild: none: the owned SubstrateMatch Python is interpreted; external compiled support remains pinned. Cross-platform evidence is not yet measured.

evidence.floor_how: No alternative build measured. Preliminary native two-ULP sensitivity is recorded in comment/native-investigation.json; it is not a platform floor.

warrant: SubstrateMatch.from_zsl forms a Green-Lagrange strain, converts its frame and multiplies elastic energy density by film volume per atom (analysis/interfaces/substrate_analyzer.py, lines 51-60). Isotropic stiffness makes the energy independent of rigid frame rotations, while explicit lattice vectors remove enumeration choices. Dropping the quadratic strain term, stiffness contraction, unit conversion or per-atom normalization changes the energy beyond the approved 1e-10 absolute plus 1e-7 relative bound. A two-ULP stretch perturbation in the native prototype changed energy by about 1.17e-15 eV/atom. This is local sensitivity evidence, not a cross-platform floor, and the user approved this bound after container calibration.
knobs: none: one fixed deformation; shortening removes the only scientific operation.
